questions.title: An iron-oxygen-complexing chemotherapy drug causing DNA strand breaks works in G2 phase
questions.question: A drug used in a chemotherapy regimen works by complexing with iron and oxygen to promote DNA strand breaks. While on this drug the patient must be monitored closely due to pulmonary side effects. In what phase of the cell cycle does this drug work?
questions.vignette: A chemotherapy drug that complexes with iron and oxygen to promote DNA strand breaks, requiring monitoring for pulmonary toxicity (a description matching bleomycin).

explanations.A: Incorrect. G1 phase is the pre-synthetic growth phase; this drug's iron-oxygen-complex DNA-strand-breaking mechanism is not maximal here.
explanations.B: Incorrect. M phase is mitosis; this drug (matching bleomycin's iron-oxygen-free-radical mechanism and pulmonary-fibrosis toxicity) is not classified as acting in M phase.
explanations.C: Incorrect. S phase is DNA synthesis; while DNA is a target, this specific iron-oxygen-complex drug is classified to act in G2, not S, phase.
explanations.D: Correct. This description matches bleomycin: it complexes with iron and oxygen to generate free radicals that cause DNA strand breaks, and carries dose-limiting pulmonary toxicity/fibrosis requiring close monitoring. Bleomycin is a cell-cycle-specific antitumour antibiotic classified as acting in the G2 phase of the cell cycle, where it blocks cells from progressing into mitosis.

questions.subtopic: Iron-oxygen-complex chemotherapy drug acting in G2 phase
questions.learning_objective: Identify the G2-phase, iron-oxygen-complex, pulmonary-toxic chemotherapy drug (bleomycin) from its mechanism and toxicity.

field_notes.keySource: printed "The correct answer is: G2 phase"

questions.title: Paclitaxel targets microtubules
questions.question: The cellular target of paclitaxel is:

explanations.A: Incorrect. Deoxyribonucleotides are the substrate targeted by antimetabolite drugs (e.g. methotrexate, 5-fluorouracil), not paclitaxel's mechanism.
explanations.B: Correct. Paclitaxel is a taxane that binds to and stabilises microtubules, preventing their normal depolymerisation. This locks the mitotic spindle in place and arrests dividing cells in mitosis, making microtubules its cellular target.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Topoisomerase is the target of drugs such as etoposide (topoisomerase II) and irinotecan (topoisomerase I), not paclitaxel.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Tyrosine kinase enzymes are the target of targeted small-molecule inhibitors (e.g. imatinib), not the cytotoxic mechanism of paclitaxel.

questions.learning_objective: Identify microtubules as the cellular target of paclitaxel.

questions.title: Cisplatin's major toxicity is nephrotoxicity rather than bone marrow suppression
questions.question: Which of the following medications has the major side effect of nephrotoxicity rather than bone marrow suppression?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Methotrexate's dose-limiting toxicity is bone marrow suppression (and mucositis), not nephrotoxicity as its major effect.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Doxorubicin's dose-limiting toxicities are bone marrow suppression and cardiotoxicity, not primarily nephrotoxicity.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Vinblastine's dose-limiting toxicity is bone marrow suppression, not nephrotoxicity.
explanations.D: Correct. Cisplatin is distinctive among common cytotoxic chemotherapy drugs for causing significant nephrotoxicity (renal tubular damage) as its major dose-limiting side effect. This contrasts with most other cytotoxic agents, such as methotrexate, doxorubicin and vinblastine, whose dose-limiting toxicity is instead bone marrow suppression. Adequate hydration is used clinically to reduce cisplatin's renal toxicity.

questions.subtopic: Cisplatin nephrotoxicity versus marrow-suppressing chemotherapy drugs
questions.learning_objective: Identify cisplatin as the chemotherapy drug whose major toxicity is nephrotoxicity rather than bone marrow suppression.

questions.title: Methotrexate is a folic acid analog
questions.question: Which of the following anticancer drugs is a folic acid analog?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Fluorouracil is a pyrimidine (uracil) analogue, not a folic acid analogue.
explanations.B: Correct. Methotrexate is a folic acid (folate) analogue. It competitively inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, blocking the regeneration of tetrahydrofolate needed for purine and thymidylate synthesis, and so halting DNA synthesis in rapidly dividing cells.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Irinotecan is a topoisomerase I inhibitor, structurally and mechanistically unrelated to folic acid.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating agent, not a folic acid analogue.

questions.subtopic: Methotrexate as a folic acid analog
questions.learning_objective: Identify methotrexate as the anticancer drug that is a folic acid analog.

questions.title: Cyclophosphamide is a cell-cycle non-specific anticancer agent
questions.question: Which of the following anticancer drugs is a cell cycle non specific agent?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Vinblastine is cell-cycle specific, acting in M phase by binding tubulin and blocking mitotic spindle formation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Methotrexate is cell-cycle specific, acting in S phase by blocking the folate pathway needed for DNA synthesis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Vincristine, like vinblastine, is cell-cycle specific, acting in M phase.
explanations.D: Correct. Cyclophosphamide is an alkylating agent. Alkylating agents are cell-cycle non-specific: they can damage DNA, by cross-linking DNA strands, in cells at any phase of the cell cycle, including non-dividing cells at rest. This is unlike the phase-restricted antimetabolites and mitotic-spindle poisons among the other options, which only act on actively cycling cells.

questions.subtopic: Cyclophosphamide as a cell-cycle non-specific alkylating agent
questions.learning_objective: Identify cyclophosphamide as a cell-cycle non-specific anticancer agent.
